annotations: Northern Virginia, 345 ways (about 99 mi), from the Virginia ratings recheck (thread "Recheck Virginia road ratings"). P4 at LTS 3.5: 8 ways (5.2 mi); P4 at LTS 4: 18 ways (5.4 mi); P5 at LTS 1.5: 252 ways (77.2 mi); P8 at LTS 2.5: 5 ways (4.6 mi); P8 at LTS 3.5: 1 way (0.6 mi); R2 at LTS 1.5: 61 ways (6.2 mi). P4 and P8 are two-lane Fairfax County streets VDOT's speed limit records post at 35 mph that OpenStreetMap carries no speed for; a way along several count blocks takes the busiest. R2 is Arlington's calmest uncounted residential streets. P3 and P6 (county-posted 25 mph streets) were withdrawn the same day by the owner ("Let the formula decide") once Virginia's urban default became 25 mph. Left out: ways the reviewed blocks cover less than half of; P4 and P8 ways OSM tags with a speed limit (the mapped sign is not overruled here), one-way, or with other than two lanes; and points where the road panel found an unnamed or differently named way, another rating than the review saw, or a bike lane. Only Fairfax ways VDOT's own speed limit layer posts at 35 mph are kept (the owner, 2026-10-31, "Keep 32, cite VDOT"): of the 71 ways Fairfax County's layer showed at 35, VDOT posts 35 on 32, 25 or 30 on 16, has no record within 20 m on 19, and mixed zones on 4; those 39 are dropped. P5 (the owner, 2026-10-31, "Keep 1.5 as owner rows"): Fairfax residential and unclassified local streets, two-way with no bike lane, at 25 mph (VDOT's posted limit, or Virginia's 25 mph residence-district law where VDOT posts none), counted by VDOT at 1,001 to 1,500 a day, at LTS 1.5; left out where VDOT posts another limit, OSM tags a speed other than 25, the way is tertiary (the collector floor), or the counted blocks cover less than half of it.

rows.reason: The owner, 2026-10-31, approving the Virginia ratings recheck: "Let's go with all these". P4: a two-lane Fairfax County street posted at 35 mph (VDOT's speed limit records), counted above 1,500 a day, was rated LTS 3 because OpenStreetMap carries no speed limit for it and the formula read a lower default. The formula with the posted 35 gives LTS 4 (35 mph mixed traffic, no low-volume relief above 1,500); on the streets where Fairfax County's bike map and this classifier agree, such streets sit between LTS 3 and LTS 4. So LTS 3.5 below 5,000 a day and LTS 4 from 5,000; a way along several count blocks takes the busiest. Kept as an owner row: the build does not yet read VDOT's speed limit layer. This way (P4): VDOT posts 35 mph on SC-674N (Fairfax County); OSM gives no speed limit and lanes tagged 2, two-way; beta rated it LTS 3; its busiest VDOT count, 2,300 a day, is over 1,500 and under 5,000, so 3.5: LTS 3.5.
